earlier_comparison.note: Frozen camera, one original character walking and moving every frame. Same motion in both modes; RT rebuilds live TLAS. raw.note: Frozen camera, one original character walking and moving every frame. Same motion in both modes; RT rebuilds live TLAS. Three interleaved rounds; not a crowded combat benchmark. RT uses four spatial samples per pixel and approximate materials; Mirror uses 2x MSAA at the same 1280x720 target.

performance.qualification: Single river scene, one animated original character, 3 interleaved rounds. Shared machine; no universal FPS claim. RT and Mirror differ in material fidelity.

limitations: Native Windows, AMD and Intel GPUs are not qualified by this run.
One planar reflected view; approximate materials; particles, shader wind, blended transparency and full global illumination are omitted.
Four fixed spatial samples reduce aliasing but do not eliminate every fine-edge artifact.
The first reflection snapshot can take several seconds; Mirror remains visible during preparation.
FSR frame generation and its additional FPS counter require first-use temporal shader preparation.
Unmodified/unsupported engines fall back to Mirror; a game pack alone cannot add the DXR engine backend.

This is a source-based attribution, not a clean native D3D12 validation result. Native Windows debug-layer qualification remains outstanding.
